content: 1. For intravenous administration of aminoglycosides, the recommended dosage is 5-7 mg/kg IV every 24 hours. Alternatively, a regimen of 2.5 mg/kg IV every 12 hours is preferred for amikacin. Note that amikacin generally demonstrates superior efficacy against Pseudomonas aeruginosa compared to tobramycin and gentamicin in most institutions. 2. In immunocompetent hosts with Salmonella gastroenteritis, antimicrobial therapy is typically not recommended for uncomplicated diarrheal illness. However, indications for antimicrobial therapy include severe disease, age over 50 years, presence of prosthetic devices, valvular heart disease, severe atherosclerosis, cancer, uremia, or immunosuppression. 3. For Salmonella gastroenteritis requiring treatment, the preferred regimens include: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) double strength (DS) orally twice daily for 5-7 days. Ciprofloxacin 500 mg orally twice daily for 5-7 days. Ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 24 hours for 5-7 days. 4. For uncomplicated typhoid fever caused by fully susceptible strains, the preferred regimen is a fluoroquinolone such as ofloxacin 15 mg/kg orally once daily for 5-7 days. For multidrug-resistant strains, the same fluoroquinolone regimen is recommended. For quinolone-resistant strains, azithromycin 8-10 mg/kg orally once daily for 7 days is preferred. Alternatively, fluoroquinolones at 20 mg/kg orally once daily for 10-14 days may be used. 5. Alternative regimens for fully susceptible typhoid fever include: Chloramphenicol 50-75 mg/kg orally once daily for 14-21 days. Amoxicillin 75-100 mg/kg orally once daily for 14 days. TMP-SMX (8 mg/kg trimethoprim and 40 mg/kg sulfamethoxazole) orally once daily for 14 days. 6. For severe typhoid fever, the preferred regimens include: Ofloxacin 15 mg/kg IV once daily for 10-14 days for fully susceptible or multidrug-resistant strains. Ceftriaxone 60 mg/kg IV once daily for 10-14 days for quinolone-resistant strains. Cefotaxime 80 mg/kg IV once daily for 10-14 days for quinolone-resistant strains. 7. For non-typhoidal Salmonella infections, the preferred regimens include third-generation cephalosporins (e.g., ceftriaxone or cefotaxime) or fluoroquinolones (e.g., ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin). 8. For bacteremia caused by Salmonella, the preferred regimens are: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 24 hours. Cefotaxime 2 g IV every 6-8 hours for 7-14 days. Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV every 12 hours for 7-14 days. 9. For vascular prosthesis infections caused by Salmonella, the preferred regimens include ceftriaxone, cefotaxime, or ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV every 12 hours for 6 weeks. 10. For osteomyelitis caused by Salmonella, the preferred regimens are: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 24 hours. Cefotaxime 2 g IV every 6-8 hours. Ciprofloxacin 750 mg orally twice daily for at least 4 weeks. 11. For arthritis caused by Salmonella, the preferred regimens include ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 24 hours or cefotaxime 2 g IV every 6-8 hours for 6 weeks. 12. For endocarditis caused by Salmonella, the preferred regimens are ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 24 hours or cefotaxime 2 g IV every 6-8 hours for 6 weeks. 13. For urinary tract infections (UTIs) caused by Salmonella, the preferred regimens include: Ciprofloxacin 250 mg orally twice daily or 400 mg IV every 12 hours. Levofloxacin 250 mg orally once daily or 500 mg IV every 24 hours. In seriously ill patients, consider empiric coverage with two drugs (e.g., a beta-lactam and an aminoglycoside or fluoroquinolones and carbapenem) until susceptibilities are known. 14. For Shigella infections in pediatric patients, the preferred regimen is ciprofloxacin 15 mg/kg orally twice daily for 3 days. Alternative regimens include pivmecillinam 20 mg/kg orally four times daily for 5 days, ceftriaxone 50-100 mg/kg intramuscularly once daily for 2-5 days, or azithromycin 6-20 mg/kg orally once daily for 1-5 days. 15. For Shigella infections in adults, the preferred regimen is ciprofloxacin 500 mg orally twice daily for 3 days. Alternative regimens include pivmecillinam 100 mg orally four times daily for 5 days or azithromycin 1-1.5 g orally once daily for 1-5 days. 16. For Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infections, the preferred treatment is TMP-SMX 15-20 mg/kg/day (TMP component) IV or orally every 8 hours. Alternative treatments include ceftazidime 2 g IV every 8 hours.
